title: Capability-based Staged Launch PRD and Acceptance Matrix for Endpoint Features
creator: Asha Patel
description: This PRD defines a capability-by-capability staged launch for the hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Goal: ship a minimal, stable public API surface while enabling rapid iteration on performance and observability. We split launch into three capability gates (Core Completions, Conversational Chat, Embeddings + Rerank) to reduce blast radius and accelerate customer feedback loops. Document covers API contracts, acceptance criteria, rollout schedule, monitoring/SLOs, migration paths and launch checklist.
scope_in_scope: Core HTTP endpoints for text completions (sync/stream) with consistent parameters across models
Conversational chat endpoint supporting streaming, function/tool calling shim, and token-level usage reporting
Embeddings endpoint supporting multiple vector sizes and L2/cosine normalization paths
Rerank endpoint that accepts candidate lists + query, returns stable scores and ranked order
Server-side defaults for batching and KV cache behavior; runtime-level SLOs applied per-route
Console pages and route-level latency/cost dashboards for each capability
SDK updates (Python + TypeScript) exposing new endpoints and streaming helpers
Canary and phased rollout controls (alpha -> private beta -> GA) with automatic fallback policies
out_of_scope: Dedicated/Dedicated capacity contracts or Dedicated-only features
Private/VPC on-prem packaging for initial GA (will be follow-up)
Full model catalog migration; this PRD assumes model variants are mapped to compatible routes
Large-scale OLAP billing analytics; only per-token and per-route nearline dashboards are required for launch
api_contract_changes: Introduce POST /v1/hosted/completions with payload fields: model, prompt, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop, stream (boolean), metadata (opaque map)
Introduce POST /v1/hosted/chat with messages array, optional functions definition, streaming support via SSE/chunked transfer
Embeddings: POST /v1/hosted/embeddings supports model and input array; returns id, vector, model, normalized_vector (when requested)
Rerank: POST /v1/hosted/rerank accepts query and candidates[]; response must include score (float 0-1) and stable_rank_id for deterministic tie-breaks
Backward compatibility: existing client parameters must map to new route equivalents; 30-day deprecation window for legacy fields
Rate limiting: per-route quota keys with soft 95th-percentile limits and hard global caps to prevent noisy neighbors
acceptance_criteria: Completions: 95th percentile latency < 250ms for short prompts (<64 tokens) on default model during GA traffic in hosted region
Completions: streaming responses maintain <150ms first-byte latency for streaming-enabled responses
Chat: function calling flow returns structured function JSON in expected schema and preserves conversation-level token accounting
Embeddings: end-to-end roundtrip for 1k inputs (avg 256 tokens) completes within target throughput baseline and embedding vectors match reference precision (within 1.5% L2 error) for quantized models
Rerank: Spearman correlation with reference reranker >= 0.88 across internal eval set; stable ranking behavior across identical inputs
SLOs: error rate < 0.1% (5xx) sustained during canary -> GA transition; automated fallback to last-stable model on detected regressions
Monitoring: dashboards show token-level cost, per-route latency percentiles, and per-model throughput; alert on 95th-latency degradation and cost-per-token delta > 15%
Security: KMS encrypted customer metadata at rest; audit log entries present for all admin actions; security review signoff recorded
Docs: API reference, SDK examples, migration guide, and sample prompts published before GA
SDKs: Python and TypeScript clients have parity for the new endpoints and streaming patterns and pass integration tests
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal Alpha): Enable endpoints behind feature flags for Redwood-internal teams and SRE; run synthetic load and collect traces (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (Partner Beta): Invite 3-5 trusted partners with production-like traffic; enable canary autoscaling and rollback automation (4 weeks)
Phase 2 (Public Beta): Open to self-serve signups with limited quota; enable public dashboards and usage analytics; monitor for regressions (6 weeks)
Phase 3 (GA): Lift quotas, publish pricing, and enable region expansion; communicate deprecation timeline for legacy endpoints (2 weeks)
Rollback policy: automated circuit breaker triggers rollback to pre-rollout model variant and notifies on-call; manual override with documented playbook
launch_checklist: Product: Final PRD approved by PM and Eng leads
Engineering: API endpoints implemented and integration tests passing in staging
Engineering: Canary deployment automation + rollback hooks validated
Design: Console UX for route dashboards and per-token breakdowns reviewed and signed off
Security: KMS/HSM integration validated and security review completed
Docs: Public API reference, migration guide, examples, and changelog entries published
SDKs: Python and TypeScript packages released with migration notes
SRE/Observability: Dashboards and alerts deployed to production monitoring stack
Billing: Pricing rules and quota enforcement configured in billing service; cost ETA validated
Sales & CS: Launch kit + FAQ + known limitations doc shared with GTM
Support: Runbook for common issues and escalation path published
Regression Tests: Perf regression set executed across top 5 latency-sensitive models
Legal/Compliance: Data processing addendum templates ready for customers requiring DPAs
monitoring_and_slo: Per-route latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 targets defined per capability (e.g., completions p95 <250ms)
Token-accurate billing telemetry exposed in console and exported to BigQuery daily
Error budget policy for GA rollouts tied to canary windows with automated pauses if budget depletion > 20%
Anomaly detection: automated drift detection on embedding distributions and sampling-based quality checks
On-call runbook: triage steps for high latency, increased error rate, and cost spikes
migration_and_deprecation_plan: 30-day deprecation for legacy fields with automatic header-based opt-in to new behavior
Migration guide with code snippets for common client libraries and a small conversion script in repo
A/B compatibility shim for 60 days to allow gradual client rollout
Telemetry to detect remaining legacy usage and automated emails to high-volume customers still using legacy parameters
docs_and_sdk_tasks: Write API reference pages for each endpoint with full request/response examples
Add streaming example notebooks (Python + Node) demonstrating partial response handling
Publish migration guide with code diffs and example prompts
Release SDK patches and coordinate with package maintainers for staged rollout
Update quickstarts and sample apps to use new host-prefixed endpoints
metrics: Adoption: number of unique API keys calling new endpoints per week
Latency: p95 response time per endpoint
Cost: average cost-per-1k-tokens per route and delta vs baseline
Quality: rerank Spearman correlation and embeddings retrieval recall@10 on internal evals
Reliability: 5xx rate and successful rollback events during rollout
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Streaming semantics differ across SDKs -> Mitigation: ship streaming compatibility layer and additional integration tests
Risk: Embedding normalization differences cause customer model drift -> Mitigation: expose both raw and normalized vectors and document recommended pipeline
Risk: Rerank instability across quantized models -> Mitigation: enforce deterministic tie-breaker and run cross-model regression tests
Risk: Cost spikes as batching rules change -> Mitigation: provide early-warning alerts and opt-out flag per-customer
Risk: Delayed security review -> Mitigation: escalate to Security leadership and block GA until signoff
comments: 2025-11-03 | Asha Patel: Initial draft circulated to Eng and Design. Requesting alignment on API surface for streaming vs chunked transfer. Action: Eng to confirm whether SSE or HTTP chunking is preferred by 2025-11-10.

2025-11-12 | Evan Brooks: Engineering prefers chunked transfer for current runtime due to easier backpressure handling. Will provide a small compatibility shim for SSE consumers. Estimated effort: 3 points.

2025-12-08 | Luca Hernández: SDK streaming PR opened (gh#402). Note: Node streaming behavior differs for large payloads; adding extra test coverage. Beta partners flagged a smaller default chunk size to avoid client OOMs.

2026-01-22 | Marta Ivanova: Canary run with internal traffic showed p95 spike at 03:15 UTC due to a misconfigured autoscaler. Mitigation: tighten scale-down threshold and add a warmup buffer. Follow-up: ENG-4239 created.
2026-02-14 | Priya Shah: Security signoff received for KMS integration; pending final documentation of audit log retention policy (target 2026-02-21).

2026-03-10 | Asha Patel: Decision log: Split GA into capability gates (completions -> chat -> embeddings+rerank) to reduce blast radius. Updated acceptance criteria to include rerank correlation threshold.
